groups.scientific_question: For the sentiment-classification comparisons, which verified dataset and model configuration yield the stated at-least-15,000-fold speedup, and what complete-training ratio follows when the baseline schedules and five fastText epochs used for the reported accuracies are included? If that ratio is not established, should the classification speedup statement be explicitly limited to single-epoch timing under the disclosed execution conditions?
Do the original task description or accompanying reconstruction materials specify exact record IDs, a deterministic assignment rule, or a random seed for the splits?
Does the original passage or surrounding material define this as expected complexity under the frequencies used to construct the Huffman tree?

Could the conclusion clarify that the demonstrated usefulness of averaged fastText features concerns the evaluated supervised classifiers, and identify the evidence or intended qualification for its contrast with averaged unsupervised word2vec vectors?
Does the complete paper provide measurements of visited nodes or runtime across class counts, rather than only the large-tag benchmark?
Do the complete experimental sections or implementation documentation specify the CPU model and the operations included in each training and test timer?
Does the complete paper distinguish end-to-end system efficiency from speed attributable to particular algorithmic components?
Does the original description or dataset script compute the frequency threshold over the whole corpus or only the training partition?
Do the complete model and tag-prediction sections specify how multiple tags are converted into training targets?
